correctness.rationale: The first 3x3 principal minor factors exactly into a two-periodic branch and a Chebyshev-recurrence branch. For an invertible leading 2x2 block, equality of columns on two rows forces an exact global column relation and hence all Toeplitz diagonals. Rank-one leading block is resolved by the 0,1,j principal minors. The t0=t1=0 projective boundary is completely excluded except for the last-corner vector by explicit nonzero 3x3 and 4x4 minors. Both parametrized families have rank<=2. Chebyshev basis gives the rational normal curve. Their two intersections u=+-1 are transverse because dT2/du=4u and the line holds t2 constant. The exact sheaf sequence gives degree n and genus1. Standalone exact polynomial and finite-field checks passed; computations support, but are not substituted for, this arbitrary-size proof. The statement carefully concerns reduced support, not the determinantal ideal scheme.

originality.rationale: The 2004 primary slides state the reducible conic-plus-line description for 3x3 Toeplitz determinants and list complicated 4x4 rank-two equations, but do not establish the 4x4-and-higher complete projective curve, Chebyshev rational-normal component, two nodes, or arithmetic genus. The 2003 structured approximation paper treats rank feasibility and optimization rather than this all-dimensional classification. The inspected Ottaviani-Spaenlehauer-Sturmfels paper treats structured approximation chiefly for other matrix families, not an all-size Toeplitz rank-two decomposition. published-finding corpus query comparisons produced only substantively unrelated records; direct claim comparison of accessible previous records found no Toeplitz rank-two geometric classification. Possible implicit recurrence-theoretic coverage remains a genuine risk.
residual_risks: Recurrence classifications in less-indexed Toeplitz matrix literature could make the union classification an implicit consequence of a more general result.
No independent expert literature audit was performed; published-finding corpus ranking and source selection do not demonstrate uniqueness.

value.rationale: The full low-rank feasible geometry of a natural structured matrix family is an all-dimensional classification, not an arbitrary finite sample or simple reformulation: it consists of a rational normal Chebyshev family plus an exceptional periodic line, glued in two nodes with arithmetic genus one. The projective boundary, components, intersections, degree and Hilbert polynomial are complete and useful for understanding identifiability and degenerations of structured low-rank matrices. The known n=3 conic/line example does not make the arbitrary-size projective classification or genus calculation a textbook substitution.
